minor.issue: Provider 'configured' logic for the sendgrid api_key mode returns configured=true unconditionally (correct per spec), but for OAuth providers it only checks client_id_env presence — a provider with client_id set but client_secret unset would falsely report configured=true. Consider `and bool(os.environ.get(client_secret_env))` too.

The API key is stored PLAINTEXT in db.oauth_tokens.access_token. The comment says 'Store encrypted (import from server if available); fallback plaintext with masking preview' but there's no encryption call. For a SendGrid key with sending scope this is a real credential-at-rest concern. Recommend using the same Fernet path that pos_secrets uses (server.py already has this pattern for POS webhook secrets).
Line 130-131 in routers/oauth_hub.py has a duplicate `cfg = PROVIDERS.get(provider)` — harmless but dead code (typo).

The dns.resolver TXT lookup uses `for a in answers` then does `''.join(a.strings[0].decode() if isinstance(a.strings[0], bytes) else a.strings[0] for _ in [0])` — the `for _ in [0]` generator is a no-op that iterates once but discards the value; this is broken TXT parsing that will not correctly match multi-string TXT records. Rewrite as `txt_value = a.strings[0].decode() if isinstance(a.strings[0], bytes) else a.strings[0]; if fid in txt_value: verified=True`.

The view_count increment `db.funnels.update_one({'slug': slug}, {'$inc': {'views': 1}})` fires on every hit including bot / crawler / rebroadcast — no rate limit or de-dup by IP+session. For a public marketing funnel this makes the 'views' counter unreliable. Consider a lightweight per-IP cool-off (or a dedicated funnel_views collection with unique index on (slug, session_id)).

Uses `LlmChat(...session_id=f'gc-{uuid.uuid4()}')` which creates a NEW ephemeral session per call — no conversation memory, no cost tracking per user. Acceptable for a one-shot copywriter, but no rate-limiting means an authenticated marketer can burn LLM budget by hammering the button. Add per-workspace rate limit (e.g., 30 calls/hour).

Not tested this iteration but code path — returns a data:image/png;base64,... URL up to several hundred KB inline in JSON. Consider streaming to /uploads then returning /api/uploads/{id} URL to keep JSON responses small and cacheable.

For a fresh diamond funnel with 4 blocks (hero, coupon, features, cta), the editor DOM shows 5 elements matching `data-testid^=block-` — the extra one is not a data-block but likely the +add-block toolbar row being caught by the prefix match. Consider a more specific data-testid like `funnel-block-{id}` on the actual block cards to disambiguate from add-block controls.

action_items: OPTIONAL (security): Encrypt OAuth/API-key tokens at rest in db.oauth_tokens.access_token — currently stored plaintext despite the code comment claiming encryption. Reuse the Fernet helper already used for POS webhook secrets in server.py.

OPTIONAL: Fix broken TXT parsing in POST /api/funnels/{fid}/verify-domain (routers/funnels.py ~line 292-297) — the `for _ in [0]` generator makes the check semantically wrong for multi-string TXT records.
OPTIONAL: Remove duplicate `cfg = PROVIDERS.get(provider)` on line 130-131 of routers/oauth_hub.py.
OPTIONAL: Add per-workspace rate-limit on POST /api/giftcards/regenerate to protect the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget from a runaway UI button-mash.
OPTIONAL (UX): Make funnel block cards use `data-testid=funnel-block-{id}` (specific) rather than `block-{id}` so the block list count is unambiguous.
OPTIONAL: For image_bg regeneration, upload the generated PNG to /uploads and return `/api/uploads/{id}` — avoids inlining hundreds of KB of base64 in JSON responses.
OPTIONAL: For 'configured' flag in /oauth/providers, also require client_secret_env to be set (not just client_id_env).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/oauth_hub.py: OAuth access tokens + API keys are stored plaintext in db.oauth_tokens.access_token — the comment says 'Store encrypted... fallback plaintext' but no encryption call exists. Real credentials at rest = real risk.
routers/oauth_hub.py line 130-131: duplicate `cfg = PROVIDERS.get(provider)` (dead code, but suggests copy-paste review discipline).

routers/funnels.py verify-domain: `for _ in [0]` is a semantic bug — the generator over `[0]` yields once but is never used; the actual TXT match logic will not correctly handle multi-string DNS TXT records.

routers/funnels.py public renderer: hydrates coupon by `db.coupons.find_one({'code': code})` WITHOUT a workspace scope — this is intentional for public pages (funnel can reference any coupon by code) BUT means a funnel author could pull in any other workspace's coupon just by knowing its code. Consider requiring the coupon block's coupon_code to belong to the funnel's own workspace_id (add workspace_id to the find_one filter) for tenant isolation.

routers/funnels.py public renderer imports `from routers.giftcards import TEMPLATES as GC_TEMPLATES` lazily inside the endpoint — works but not idiomatic. Prefer a top-level import; there is no circular dependency risk here.
routers/giftcards.py regenerate: no rate-limit / no cost tracking — a runaway UI button can burn EMERGENT_LLM_KEY quota. Add a lightweight per-workspace counter (e.g., MongoDB TTL doc).

routers/giftcards.py: image_bg returns a base64 data URL up to ~500KB inline in JSON. Prefer uploading to /uploads (already implemented) and returning /api/uploads/{id} for cache-ability + smaller payloads.

server.py is now 2777+ lines and still not split despite recommendations in iter-5/6/7/8 test reports. The router split in iter-9 addressed extras.py and added routers/{giftcards,oauth_hub,funnels}.py — GOOD progress. Recommend the follow-up split: auth, coupons, campaigns, pos_webhooks, journeys, ai_copy, analytics, exports, embed, customers, admin, library, api_keys.

routers/funnels.py list endpoint returns FULL funnel doc including all blocks — for a workspace with 100 funnels this can be a heavy response. Consider a lightweight `?summary=true` mode that omits `blocks` array for the list view.

routers/oauth_hub.py publish endpoint (POST /oauth/{provider}/publish) is essentially a stub — it stores intent in db.social_posts but doesn't call the provider's real POST API. Explicitly acknowledged in the code comment ('The full provider POST is out-of-scope for this iteration') but users will see 'queued' status forever with no worker. Consider explicit UI messaging on the Integrations page: 'Publishing requires production API approval from {provider} — connection only for now.'
routers/oauth_hub.py callback: state token stored in db.oauth_states has no TTL — expired states pile up forever. Add a MongoDB TTL index on `created_at` with `expireAfterSeconds: 600`.
